During a hardworking shift, we are glad to have your thoughts; we looked into it and understand that your complaint concerns the handling of your companion animal, the clarity of boarding guidance, and the assurance that welfare would be protected throughout the journey. We acknowledge that such matters are sensitive, and the desk must treat them with calm attention, careful review, and clear communication at every stage. Safety takes priority over speed in every journey. A welfare coordinator reviews animal comfort needs. When a traveler raises concern, our first duty is to check whether the animal was screened, handled, and transferred in a manner consistent with approved practice. We also review whether staff gave practical instructions in plain language, because uncertainty at the counter or gate can add avoidable stress for both traveler and animal.

In this case, the proper response is to strengthen the handoff between the service desk, the ramp team, and the cabin team so that each step is confirmed before movement begins. The traveler should not be left to infer what will happen next, and the animal should not be exposed to unnecessary noise, delay, or repeated transfers. We have reinforced the expectation that staff explain crate placement, document any comfort notes, and record any exception promptly so that the next team can act without hesitation. If a carrier, harness, or comfort item needs review, the matter must be addressed before acceptance rather than after departure.

For future journeys, we advise travelers to present the animal early, keep identification current, and share any welfare needs in advance so the desk can coordinate support. Our staff will continue to review reports, correct weak points in handling, and improve the consistency of service at Aurelia Skyways. The Companion Animal Travel Desk remains responsible for ensuring that concern is met with action, not routine reassurance alone. We regret the distress described and will use the report to support safer, clearer, and more respectful service on later travel. Companion Animal Travel Desk
